label: Colossians attests Christians at Phrygian Hierapolis

date.note: Traditional Pauline dating from an imprisonment (c. 55–62), which Harnack assumes. If Colossians is deutero-Pauline the letter shifts to c. 70–80, still pre-Trajan.

secondary.cite: Harnack, Mission and Expansion, vol. 2, pp. 185–186

notes: Phrygian Hierapolis at Pamukkale (Pleiades 638860), not the several homonyms; the Lycus-valley city grouped with Colossae and Laodicea. Attested only indirectly: Col 4.13 says Epaphras laboured for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis. Weaker than a named addressee.
